sections.title: Vision & Values
sections.statement: To enhance and expand learning opportunities for Western Australian students, regardless of their circumstances, through high quality, inclusive and culturally responsive educational programs in a blended learning environment.

frames.title: Courage
frames.body: Students are encouraged to take bold steps in their learning, embracing new challenges and showing resilience when faced with change. Through persistence and self-belief, they grow the confidence to share their voices and stories, valuing both their own perspectives and those of others.

frames.title: Connection
frames.body: Strong relationships form the heart of learning. Students, teachers, and communities stay connected through collaboration, respect, and shared purpose, honouring the importance of belonging that is deeply valued in Aboriginal cultures and across all learning communities.

frames.title: Equity
frames.body: Every student is given fair access to quality education, regardless of location or circumstance. Teaching practices are inclusive and culturally aware, recognising the diverse identities, languages, and experiences that shape each learner’s journey.

frames.title: Creativity
frames.body: Innovation and imagination guide learning across all subjects. Students explore new ideas and express themselves through digital and cultural forms, reflecting Australia’s diverse heritage and the creative strength of its communities.

frames.title: Compassion
frames.body: Empathy and understanding are embedded in every interaction. Students learn to listen with care, act with kindness, and support one another, fostering a culture that values respect, shared wellbeing, and the stories that connect us all.

sections.title: History
sections.lead: Explore the rich and varied past of a school over 100 years old.

entries.title: Early 1918
entries.text: C. Andrews attended a Melbourne conference discussing education for outback children in Western Australia. On return to WA, Andrews recommended establishing a Correspondence School to serve students living far from local schools.

entries.title: September 1918
entries.text: The Correspondence School opened in a house on St George’s Terrace with two appointed teachers.

entries.title: First Enrolments
entries.text: Initial enrolments quickly grew to 73 students aged five to sixteen. Demand exceeded expectations, prompting expansion of materials and marking cycles.

entries.title: Relocation Near Government Printer
entries.text: Administrative offices moved near the Government Printer in Murray Street.

entries.title: Duplicating Lessons
entries.text: Typed masters were duplicated to speed lesson dispatch. Use of duplicators improved consistency and reduced turnaround times.

entries.title: Teacher Networks
entries.text: Correspondence teachers formed subject networks to standardise marking.

entries.title: Depression-Era Relief Lessons
entries.text: Simplified lesson packs reduced postage weight and printing costs. Standardised worksheets replaced some hand-typed materials to maintain continuity during budget contractions.

entries.title: Post-War Reorganisation
entries.text: Returned service teachers filled vacancies across remote districts.

entries.title: Radio Tutorials Begin
entries.text: Scheduled radio sessions supplemented mailed coursework. Studios broadcast weekly tutorials to reduce isolation and clarify complex topics.

entries.title: Photocopiers Adopted
entries.text: Stencil duplicators were replaced by early photocopiers.

entries.title: Audio Cassette Packs
entries.text: Subject packs included cassettes for language and science demonstrations. Playback instructions were printed on card inserts to standardise usage.

entries.title: Computer-Based Typing
entries.text: Word processors replaced typewriters in materials production.

entries.title: Early Web Pages
entries.text: Course outlines and forms were published on a public website. Static HTML pages reduced phone enquiries and provided downloadable enrolment forms.

entries.title: Learning Management System
entries.text: An LMS piloted online quizzes and digital submissions.

entries.title: Video Conferencing Rollout
entries.text: Live classes were scheduled across multiple time zones. Attendance tracking and recordings integrated with the LMS for revision.

entries.title: Remote Learning Scale-Up
entries.text: Additional servers and support channels handled a surge in online enrolments. Guides for families and device setup checklists were distributed digitally.

entries.title: 2025 Design System Refresh
entries.text: Unified styles for colour, typography and components were deployed across sites.
